query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: average_component_rating
per_column.rationale: This is an aggregate summary of all the service quality components rolled into one number. It restates the whole concept (mean of the parts) rather than isolating a single constitutive aspect of it.

per_column.name: rating_variance
per_column.rationale: Dispersion across component ratings is a meta-property describing consistency/agreement of the ratings, not an aspect OF service quality itself (e.g., comfort, staff, food). It measures how spread out the scores are, not a part of the concept.

per_column.name: satisfaction_group
per_column.rationale: A discretized bucket of overall satisfaction. This is a re-expression of the aggregate quality/outcome, not a distinct constitutive facet of service quality.

per_column.name: is_complaint_review
per_column.rationale: A binary derived from overall low quality/dissatisfaction. It flags the outcome of poor quality rather than decomposing quality into an aspect of it.

judge.rationale: None of the added columns are constitutive facets (part-of aspects) of airline_service_quality. The genuine facets already exist in the original table (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Inflight Entertainment, Value For Money). The added columns are instead aggregates/restatements of the whole (average_component_rating, satisfaction_group, is_complaint_review) or a meta-statistical property of the ratings (rating_variance). Because the set contains no true facets, exhaustiveness is 0. Mutual exclusivity is low as well: average_component_rating, satisfaction_group, and is_complaint_review are all near-collinear re-expressions of overall quality/satisfaction, capturing the same underlying dimension under different names.
